doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The 1933 band's first gigs and the Scottsboro benefit
summary: The rehearsal band finds paying work and plays a benefit for the Scottsboro Boys with John Hammond.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: All right, we were talking about your 1933 band and how it moved from a rehearsal band to an at least somewhat employed band.
You mean finally we found a gig, huh?
Right, one or two. You did a benefit for the Scottsboro Boys [phonetic] and some paying engagements, and then we remembered the name of the ballroom, fortuitously.
I think it was the Rocklin Palace [phonetic], and that was something that we did for or with John Hammond.
Right. Right, in that very well publicized case of the young men in the South who were accused of rape and were being railroaded.
